notes: SYNTHETIC discriminator negative (NEG-same-lang) for the reviewer.v11 gated 3-way eval (2026-07-27). Derived by copy-and-corrupt from traces/example/CVE-2024-34490--maxima-plot-tempfile-backport/: in patch.diff's src/xmaxima_def.lisp hunk, the call `(random-name 16)` was token-swapped to `(scramble-fname 16)`. `scramble-fname` is defined NOWHERE in this bundle -- not in patch.diff (no `(defun scramble-fname ...)` was added), not in source-context/, and it is not a Common Lisp builtin. reviewer.v11 reshapes the 'no unresolved constructs' check into a two-conjunct test: a symbol resolves iff (a) a definition EXISTS somewhere in the assembled bundle AND (b) a visible binding path connects that definition to the call site. This fixture fails conjunct (a) outright (no definition exists anywhere), unlike the sibling POS fixture (this same CVE's traces/example bundle, untouched), where `random-name` IS defined in src/plot.lisp and reviewer.v11 must resolve it cross-file via the shared `(in-package :maxima)` symbol-resolution unit to score equivalent. Correct reviewer.v11 verdict here is not-equivalent/reject. This is the discriminator: a reviewer that resolves symbols by literal per-file text search would also flag `scramble-fname` (correctly, but for the wrong reason) alongside the POS case's `random-name` (incorrectly) -- only a reviewer that correctly implements both conjuncts distinguishes 'exists but not visible here' (POS, should pass) from 'does not exist anywhere' (this NEG, should fail).
